newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish finmin sees limited flood economic impact.
newsitem.headline: Polish finmin sees limited flood economic impact.

text.p: Polish Finance Minister Marek Belka said on Wednesday that July's heavy flooding was unlikely to significantly affect the economy's momentum or contribute to strong inflationary pressure.
"The Polish economy is like a rushing locomotive, which the flood will not be able to stop," Belka told a news conference.
He based his optimism on excellent revenues in July from corporate tax, which would have been much worse had the flood caused more severe damage to the economy.

"There is a possiblity that in the first two months we will see a slowdown because growth of industrial production will be somewhat smaller. But in a long-term perspective I foresee no statistically significant GDP slowdown," he said.

The central bank's president Hanna Gronkiewicz-Waltz has said the flood was likely to cut GDP growth by up to one percentage point. The government's official GDP growth forecast is 5.5 percent for 1997.
He reiterated pledges to finance the reconstruction of areas hit by the flood in such a way so as to cause as little inflation as possible.
He said the finance ministry would limit the use of the 2.5-billion zloty ($720.9 million) loan earmarked from the central bank for relief operations.

"We know today that we are not going to take advantage of the whole of the credit," Belka said. Nothing had yet been spent from the one billion zlotys already drawn on the credit, he said, adding it would not be used if there was no need to do so.
